releases.name: v0.4.2 — activate Jev latest alias
releases.body: Fixes the OpenRouter Decisions model identifier to use the `~typesafe/jev-latest` moving alias. This makes Jev the actual primary classifier instead of immediately falling back to the chat classifier.\n\nVerified with the full test suite, build, package dry-run, and live OpenRouter gateway probes returning `classifier: "jev"`.

releases.name: v0.4.1 — executable gateway hotfix
releases.body:
This hotfix preserves the executable mode and npm bin mapping for switchyard-gateway. It also adds a manifest regression test and a clean npm publish dry-run check before release.

All Jev-first classifier functionality from v0.4.0 is included.

releases.name: v0.4.0 — Jev-first classification
releases.body:
Switchyard now uses TypeSafe Jev through OpenRouter Decisions as its primary remote task classifier. Invalid, unavailable, or low-confidence decisions fall back to the existing chat classifier and then to local keyword classification.

This release also adds bounded decision caching and outage cooldowns, keeps explicit task constraints authoritative, excludes decision-only models from execution, adds deterministic classifier evaluation, and documents the remote-classification privacy boundary.

See CHANGELOG.md for the complete release notes.

## Fixed

- Align keyword uncertainty with all six complexity boundaries.
- Preserve Pi/OMP admission decisions with explicit notify, escalate, and ignore policies.
- Route with live host context/tool constraints and optional operator constraints.
- Smooth verified outcome history by sample size, recency, complexity, and privacy-safe project scope.

Closes #5, #6, #7, and #8.

## Fixed

- Keep cold-start benchmark priors separate from measured outcome history.
- Refresh Pi/OMP catalog and Codex capacity during long-running sessions.
- Learn model quality only from explicit failures and verified outcomes.

## Added

- Add opt-in Pi/OMP routing through `switchyard/auto`, including OMP prewalk handoffs.
- Add commands to mark the last routed run as verified successful or failed.
